title: Sunset Scheduler with Tamper‑Evident Audit Chain and Recovery Window
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers require an auditable, timezone-aware mechanism to schedule data sunsets that: 1) enforces retention windows per tenant and geo, 2) allows short-term recovery if a legal hold is placed after a sunset window (a configurable recovery window), and 3) emits tamper-evident deletion evidence that customers can download or push to their compliance systems. Current deletion exports are ad-hoc and do not provide immutable proof artifacts or simulation tooling to estimate cost/volume before policy enforcement.

Scope: Implement a Sunset Scheduler service and UI flow that: (a) applies tenant/geo retention rules to mark records for soft-delete, (b) supports a configurable recovery period (rehydration window) during which operators or legal holds can pause/compress deletion, (c) generates a Merkle-chain style deletion ledger and per-tenant manifest signed by Redwood KMS for verifiable proof, (d) provides a retention-simulator to model expected token/row volume and cost impact before rolling policies live, and (e) exposes an evidence-exporter API and a customer-facing export bundle (zip + signed manifest) that includes a human-readable timeline and machine-verifiable checksums.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: deep archival storage changes, on-prem installer packaging, and full console redesign. Those will be follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Retention rules can be defined per-tenant and per-region in the console and saved as a policy
Sunset Scheduler marks eligible records as 'soft_deleted' at the configured local midnight respecting tenant timezone
A configurable recovery window (0-30 days) exists; records within the window can be rehydrated with an audit note
Deletion evidence bundle generated after final expunge contains: manifest.json, signed_merkle_root.txt, per-file checksums, and human timeline.pdf
Evidence bundle is signed with Redwood KMS key and verification steps are documented in /docs/compliance/sunset-verification.md
Retention-simulator produces a monthly projected token/row deletion volume and cost delta given a sample workload or historic traces
API endpoint /v1/compliance/evidence-export accepts tenant_id and range and returns a pre-signed URL for the bundle
Integration tests cover scheduler run, rehydrate API, and signature verification flow
Emails/notifications are sent to configured tenant contacts when a final expunge has completed
tasks: Design data model for soft_delete + recovery_window flags (ENG collaboration)
Scheduler cron implementation respecting tenant timezone + DST edge cases
Build KMS signing pipeline for evidence bundles (eng + security)
Retention-simulator prototype that replays 90 days of traces to estimate deletions
Console: policy authoring UI with preview and 'simulate' button
Evidence-exporter API + customer portal download flow
End-to-end integration tests and a verification utility (CLI)
risks: Large-scale final expunge could cause IO spikes; need throttling and backoff
Timezone/DST bugs could cause off-by-one-day deletions in some regions
KMS key rotation must not invalidate old evidence bundles; include key versioning in manifest
Legal hold race conditions when a hold is placed concurrently with an expunge run
Simulator accuracy depends on representativeness of sample traces; mis-simulation could surprise customers
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Launch retention-simulator and policy authoring in console behind feature flag (internal only) - run for 2 weeks
Phase 2: Soft-launch Sunset Scheduler for test tenants with recovery_window defaults set to 14 days
Phase 3: Enable evidence-exporter and KMS signing; invite 3 pilot customers for feedback
Phase 4: Gradual ramp to all tenants with rate limits and monitoring; provide opt-out for immediate expunge
Post-launch: 30-day stabilization, capture operational metrics, and refine throttling heuristics
